subject: Follow-up: deployment mode clarification + hosted pilot options
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex@parcelly.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: deployment mode clarification + hosted pilot options

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our side and a couple of clarifying asks so we can recommend the right evaluation path (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC):

What we covered:
- Parcelly's goal: conversational support and generation features inside the app (routing, summary, and assisted responses).
- Primary concerns: latency, cost predictability, and EU data residency.
- Demo notes: streamed responses, function-calling examples, and an initial estimate of expected volume (very rough).

Clarifying questions to help us recommend a pilot path:
1) Target SLOs: what 95th/99th latency target are you aiming for (ms)?
2) Traffic profile: can you share an expected peak requests-per-second (or tokens/day) for the first 90 days? A simple CSV with hourly QPS or a short bullet estimate works.
3) Data sensitivity: will the requests include regulated PII or PCI data that cannot leave EU tenancy?
4) Integration constraints: do you require a VPC peering/private endpoint or is a hosted EU region acceptable for pilot?

Initial recommendation (if you want the fastest time-to-value): Hosted EU pilot. We can provision a sandbox endpoint in the eu-west region, provide a short quickstart playbook, and set conservative rate caps that you can ramp. Hosted lets you validate latency/quality quickly without procurement for Dedicated or Private.

If you need strict data residency and no cross-border egress, we’ll surface the Private VPC option (longer lead time, but meets residency/SOC requirements). Dedicated is the middle ground for predictable throughput and contractual commits.

Proposed next steps:
- You: send an _approximate_ traffic profile and confirm residency requirement (yes/no).
- We: provision a hosted EU sandbox endpoint, share the "EU-hosted-quickstart-playbook.pdf" and an endpoint SLA spreadsheet, and propose a 2-week pilot config with rate caps.

I can have Monica (ops) scope the sandbox once we get the traffic numbers.

Thanks —
Olga
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment stubs: EU-hosted-quickstart-playbook.pdf (guide), endpoint-sla-matrix.csv (SLA and rate guidance)
From: Alex Rivera <alex@parcelly.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: eng+infra@parcelly.com
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 09:18:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Follow-up: deployment mode clarification + hosted pilot options

Thanks, Olga — good summary. A few answers below.

1) Latency SLOs: we need 95th < 500ms for user-facing chat, 99th ideally < 900ms. Anything above that causes noticeable UI lag.
2) Traffic profile (initial 90 days):
   - Typical steady-state: ~200 requests/hour (mostly non-peak) during MVP testing.
   - Peak during daytime support windows: up to ~3,000 requests/hour (≈0.83 RPS).
   - Token estimate: ~1.2M tokens/day at peak (mix of short prompts + 700-1,500 token completions).
3) Data sensitivity: customer PII will appear in prompts (names, addresses). We need EU residency for customer data; ideally data must not be persisted outside EU.
4) Integration constraints: for the pilot we'd prefer hosted EU region if you can guarantee that customer payloads remain in the EU and satisfy SOC2 controls. Long-term we may require VPC/private deployment depending on audit outcomes.

Questions for you: what initial rate caps would you propose for the sandbox endpoint to emulate our peak behavior safely? Also, can you confirm whether logs or audit exports for the hosted pilot can be restricted to an EU storage account?

If hosted is feasible for pilot under EU-only residency and audit log controls, we’re happy to start with that and revisit Dedicated/VPC by the end of the quarter.

Best,
Alex Rivera
VP Product | Parcelly
alex@parcelly.com

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: deployment mode clarification + hosted pilot options

Alex — appreciate the detail, that helps a lot. Short answers and a concrete pilot plan below.

EU residency and logs
- We can run a hosted sandbox in eu-west with physical processing and log retention scoped to EU-only storage. For SOC2-level evidence we'd surface audit logs and sign an addendum in the pilot agreement. If the audit requires customer-managed keys/HSM in-region, that would push toward Private VPC.

Suggested sandbox rate caps (to emulate your peak safely):
- Default rate cap: 20 requests/sec (RPS) per endpoint
- Burst allowance: up to 50 RPS for short spikes (token-based throttling applies)
- Concurrent streams: 4 concurrent streaming connections
- Token cap: 5M tokens/day for the sandbox (can be lowered/upgraded programmatically)

Why these numbers: they let you test the 95th/99th latency envelope under signficant load while keeping cost and capacity predictable. Given your peak token estimate (~1.2M/day), the sandbox token cap is a safe multiple for stress testing.

Pilot plan (2 weeks):
1) We provision: Hosted EU sandbox endpoint (hosted-staging-eu.parcelly.redwood.ai) + API key + restricted audit-log export to EU bucket.
2) You provide: a simple hourly traffic CSV or sample replay (we can provide a small script to replay).
3) Day 1–3: integration + smoke tests (ramping to 20 RPS).
4) Day 4–10: sustained replay testing targeting 95th latency measurement and correctness checks.
5) Day 11–14: run canary production-like slices and review results; decide whether to continue hosted or move to Dedicated/VPC.

Files attached (stubs): EU-hosted-quickstart-playbook.pdf — step-by-step for the sandbox, including sample curl and SDK calls; endpoint-sla-matrix.csv — mapping of rate caps to expected latency percentiles on eu-west.

Next steps:
- Alex: confirm you’re OK with the sandbox token cap and burst behavior, and share the traffic CSV (or tell us if you’d like us to provide the replay script).
- Olga/Monica: we’ll provision the sandbox once we get the CSV and a signed pilot T&Cs (I’ll draft a short one-pager).

If you prefer, I’m available for a 30-minute ops call to walk through endpoint configs and EU audit export.

Thanks —
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com

Attachment stubs: EU-hosted-quickstart-playbook.pdf, endpoint-sla-matrix.csv
